scenes.title: Where every entry goes
beats: Saturday night. Ramesh asks one question about Green Villa: is it making money?
For three weeks, people have entered what they did. Ravi's mornings and evenings, Anil's orders, Meera's bills. Nobody has typed a total.
This episode follows those entries to the answer, and back down again: from the margin to the line, and from the line to the message that made it.

lines.text: Entries → BOQ lines → cost control → P&L
And back down: margin → line → message

scenes.title: How a builder knows
beats: The BOQ is the yardstick. Each line says what a unit of work should cost: labour, material, and what the client pays for it.
So every piece of work done earns its share of the budget. Plaster forty square metres, and the line has earned forty times its rates.
Against that, what was really spent: the crew that day, the cement that went into it. Earned against spent, line by line, is the real margin.

The books are different. They count bills: what was billed to the client against what was paid out. Work done and not billed yet makes the books look worse than the job. Both are true; they answer different questions.

scenes.title: One entry, many pages
beats: Take one of Ravi's evenings: plastering, sixteen square metres, six masons and helpers, cement used.
The work lands on the BOQ's plastering line: it earns. The attendance lands on the same line: labour spent. The cement leaves the store: material used.
From there it is read by every page after it: Green / red, Budget vs actual, Materials vs BOQ, the forecast, the P&L, and Ramesh's Home.
Ravi entered it once, on WhatsApp. Everything else is that entry, read again.

scenes.title: A line goes red
beats: Thursday morning. Anil has counted yesterday's work on the BOQ. He opens Green / red for Green Villa, this week so far: Monday to Wednesday.
Plastering at the Main block is red: ten thousand rupees of work earned, fifteen thousand of labour spent. Five thousand over in three days.
One tap on the line, and the figures open into their entries: three days of sixteen square metres each, with a full crew every day.
The site's notes say why: walls chased for conduits missed on the first pass, plastered again. The crew was busy. Most of it was rework.

scenes.title: The cement says the same
beats: The cement tells the same story from the other side.
Materials vs BOQ sets what was used against what the work done should have used, from the BOQ's materials per unit.

Blocks, steel, aggregate: within what the work needed. Cement and sand: more. A hundred and ninety-four bags used where the work done needed a hundred and twenty-eight: a full day's mortar on days that did less than half a day's new work.

frames.show: cement: used against what the work needed

scenes.title: What Anil does about it
beats: Seeing it is half of it. Anil acted the same day it went red.
A task for Ravi: mark every conduit point before the next room is plastered. Ravi has it on his list, due today.
And Rahim's helpers at the Main block cut from four to two for the rest of the plastering: the work left does not need a full gang.

scenes.title: Back within the line
beats: A week later. The plastering is finished, with the smaller gang, and no wall done twice.
Green / red: plastering green again. The rework is still in the line's to-date figures; it is not hidden, it just stopped growing.
That is the whole loop: entered, noticed, acted on, and seen to work.

scenes.title: Is it making money?
beats: Day thirty-one. Green Villa's running bill went to Dr. Anand Krishnan yesterday. Ramesh opens the project's P&L.
The books: billed against what was paid out, eight percent. They lag, because twenty-three lakh rupees of work is done and not billed yet.

The real margin: the work done at its rates against what it cost, fourteen and a half percent. And at finish: sixty-three lakh against a budget of sixty-two, seventy-two thousand over. The plastering rework is in it, and it stopped growing.
From any of these figures he can go down: to Budget vs actual, to the line, to the entries, to Ravi's message. That is what entering everything buys him.

scenes.title: Five ways the numbers lie
beats: Five ways the numbers lie.
Work and labour on no BOQ line: cost control cannot see them, so a line looks fine while the money is going somewhere nobody looks.
Reading the books as the real margin: a job that is fine, looking like a loss, because it was not billed.
A forecast from three days of work. Mesiri waits until a tenth of the budget is earned.
And noticing at the month's end what Green / red shows the same day.

footer.text: Enter it once, on its line. Then every page can be trusted.

scenes.title: Three questions
beats: Three questions. Pause, and answer them before you go on.
One: what does a piece of work earn? Its quantity times its BOQ line's rates.
Two: the books say eight percent, the real margin fourteen and a half. Which is right? Both: the books count bills, and twenty-three lakh of work is not billed yet.
Three: plastering went red. How did Anil know why? He tapped the line: the work on it, the crew on it, and the site's notes.
Next: billing the client. Turning the work done into money in the bank.
